# Rank-six directions with eight deletions

## Statement

Use the pinned P112 labels `ell(t)` in `F2^9` and doubled E8 root
representatives `r_t` in `Q^8`. For a label subspace `V`, write
`Lambda(V) = {t : ell(t) in V}`. For a nonzero direction `h`, write
`Off(h) = {t : r_t dot h != 0}`.

**Finite theorem.** Fix any two six-dimensional label subspaces `V1,V2`.
The real projective directions `h` for which there exists a set `D_h` of at
most eight lines satisfying

```
rank_F2 ell(Off(h) \ (Lambda(V1) union Lambda(V2) union D_h)) <= 6
```

number at most three. Their real span therefore has dimension at most three.
The dimension bound also holds over every characteristic-zero coefficient
field, and when the deletion set is required to be common to all directions.
The count of three and span of three are attained in the separately chosen
`D_h` model. No common-set attainment is asserted.

The full finite replay proves this statement on the exact labels. The
root-system argument below proves that its finite direction list is complete.
This is a scoped decoder lemma, not a supplier or multiplication theorem.

## Direction completeness and flat capacity

The replay enumerates all 788,035 three-dimensional annihilators in `F2^9`
by reduced row echelon form. Every six-dimensional label flat is their
kernel. It checks that every such flat contains at most 20 P112 labels.
Thus an admissible direction satisfies

```
|Off(h)| <= 20 + 20 + 8 + 20 = 68.
```

The last 20 bounds the residual rank-six label set, enlarged to a six-flat.
At least 44 of the 112 root lines are perpendicular to `h`.

The root-subsystem classification used in the predecessor now has a short
specialization. A simply laced root subsystem of rank at most six has at most
36 root lines. A rank-seven subsystem other than E7 has at most 42. Hence
the perpendicular subsystem is E7. Its one-dimensional normal is an E8 root
line, so only the 120 E8 root projective directions can occur. Eight are the
removed frame directions and 112 are P112 roots. Their P112 supports have
sizes 56 and 53 respectively. This uses the same ADE/E8 fact as
`research/one-sided-six-multisets/README.md`, section 4, rather than assuming
that a finite short-vector search covers arbitrary directions.

For a characteristic-zero field, the at least 44 rational root vectors have
the same rank after scalar extension. Their rank-seven perpendicular system
has a one-dimensional kernel generated by a rational root normal. Thus no
new projective directions appear after extending the coefficient field.

## Exact finite coverage

The new implementation uses none of the predecessor search or rank routines.
`geometry.py` reconstructs all roots and labels with exact rational elimination
in the stated E8 simple-root basis. It checks the reconstruction against the
pinned source header. It also verifies that all twelve source permutations
are label-linear and permute the 120 distinct root-support masks.

`census.cpp` constructs all annihilators independently by RREF. Deduplicating
the nonempty `Lambda` masks leaves 776,805 masks. Union-find under the twelve
verified permutations partitions them into 159 orbits. Any subgroup suffices:
its transformations preserve all label ranks and permute the complete direction
set. Taking one first-flat representative and every second flat therefore
covers every pair. The replay checks 123,511,995 representative pairs.

An empty `Lambda` mask may be omitted in either slot. One remaining six-flat,
one residual six-flat and eight deletions cover at most 48 lines, below the
minimum nonzero support of 53. Empty masks cannot qualify a direction.

For each first-flat mask, the direction is discarded only if its remaining
support exceeds `40+p`. For each second flat, it is discarded only if its
remaining support exceeds `20+p`. Both are necessary cardinality bounds.
Every surviving test is decided by the exact dual-code oracle below.
The complete `p=8` result has maximum three directions, 71,726 positive flat
pairs and 3,298,476 oracle calls. All 159 rows are retained in `RESULT.json`.
The independent `p=4` control reproduces the predecessor maximum of one,
with 286 positive pairs and 69,064 oracle calls. The predecessor's `p=4`
claim had one implementation; this control is a separate implementation.

## Dual-code deletion oracle

Let `S` be the residual set of distinct labels and let its binary rank be `r`.
If `r<=6`, no deletion is necessary. Otherwise put `k=r-6`, which is at most
three. Each ambient character `x in F2^9` defines the support mask

```
C_x = {t in S : x dot ell(t) = 1}.
```

**Oracle lemma.** There is a deletion set of size at most `p` leaving rank at
most six if and only if `k` linearly independent nonzero character masks have
union size at most `p`.

For the forward implication, choose `k` independent linear forms on `span(S)`
that vanish on the retained span. They extend to ambient characters. Their
support union lies within the deleted set. Conversely, the common kernel of
`k` independent forms has dimension `r-k=6` and contains every undeleted label.
Mask deduplication quotients out the annihilator of `span(S)` and preserves
linear independence. Each selected mask must individually have size at most
`p`, so filtering by that size loses no solution.

The code enumerates all 511 nonzero ambient characters. Distinct nonzero masks
form an independent pair. For three distinct nonzero masks, independence is
exactly the condition that the third is not the XOR of the first two. This
replaces the predecessor's recursive basis-hitting deletion search. The
cardinality bound needs no real-rank arithmetic. The executable compares the oracle with all
literal deletion subsets on 4,096 twelve-line fixtures at every budget from
zero through eight, for 36,864 comparisons. Positive certificates include
actual deletion masks, checked again with a separate Python XOR-span engine.

## Mixed-rank transfer

Retain the hypotheses of the pinned TWOSIDE reduction. Let `B` be a basis of
low pieces `q_i`, let `T=span(B)`, and let `C` be the P112 root code. Every
nonzero codeword in `C` has support at least 53. Let `n=|B|=rho+b` and assume
`d=dim(T intersect C)>=b`, as supplied by the two-sided deletion lemma.
The quotient map is `lambda:T -> T/(T intersect C)`.

Choose `rho` pieces `X0` whose combined support has fewer than 53 lines.
Their quotient images are independent: a nonzero linear combination lies in
`T` and has that small support, so it cannot belong to `C`. The quotient has
dimension `n-d<=rho`, hence these images are a quotient basis and `d=b`.
The predecessor's fundamental-circuit Lemma B then gives `b` independent
codeword directions `h_y`, one for every `y in B\X0`, with

```
Off(h_y) subset union_{x in X0} supp(q_x) union supp(q_y).
```

Suppose the basis support is covered by two six-flats and at most eight
additional lines. Every nonbasis piece of weight at most six supplies an
admissible direction in the finite theorem. If `s7` nonbasis pieces have weight
seven, their directions add at most `s7` dimensions. Consequently

```
b <= 3 + s7.
```

All assumptions are needed. This is not a statement about every low piece
configuration or an unconditional decoder floor.

## Closing the stated (5,3) beta residue

An independent multiset enumeration reproduces the four shapes remaining after
the pinned necessary size/cap constraints and BK/BK7 filters. Here the weight
of a zero-excess piece is conservatively replaced by two, exactly as in the
predecessor. This enlarges the permitted support/rank bounds and cannot create
a false exclusion. There are 2,793 multisets in the bounded enumeration.

| Weights in the eight-piece basis | Chosen quotient basis | Support cap | Extra lines | Nonbasis sevens | Direction bound |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `2,6^7` | `2,6,6` | 42 | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| `2,6^6,7` | `2,6,6` | 42 | 2 | 1 | 4 |
| `3,6^7` | `3,6,6` | 44 | 4 | 0 | 3 |
| `4,5,6^6` | `4,6,6` | 48 | 8 | 0 | 3 |

The two weight-six pieces fit the two six-flats. The remaining chosen piece
has at most 2, 4 or 8 support lines. Each support cap is strictly below 53,
so the quotient argument applies. Every direction bound is below the five
independent directions required by Lemma B. All four shapes are excluded.

The `p=2,R=7` result already excludes the first two shapes. The recorded
`p=4,R=6` result already implies the third. The new `p=8,R=6` theorem supplies
the missing small-piece coverage for `4,5,6^6`, and a uniform independently
checked argument for the whole stated cell. The older four-survivor note is
not treated as the latest frontier for those first three shapes.

Other beta cells, C1-C7 as a whole, and `C(P112)>=64` remain unresolved by this
package. No selected result, supplier word, physical invoice or kappa changes.
